claims.text: Randomly distributed constituents with differing atomic sizes produce severe lattice distortion in multi-component concentrated alloys.
Severe lattice distortion forces edge-dislocation cores away from their neutral planes.
Displaced edge-dislocation cores form wavy dislocation lines.
Wavy dislocation lines reduce dislocation mobility.
The distortion-induced edge-dislocation behavior, rather than conventional screw-dislocation behavior, governs alloy strength and deformation.
NbTaTiV is a single-phase BCC refractory multi-component concentrated alloy.
The cited NbTaTiV material was produced by arc melting and homogenization.
NbTaTiV exhibits significant lattice distortion because its components have large atomic-size differences.
Selecting chemically similar elements with closer atomic sizes will reduce lattice distortion while retaining a BCC phase.
Compression at approximately 1 × 10^-4 s^-1 from room temperature through 900°C is an experimentally demonstrated test regime for NbTaTiV.
Severe lattice distortion creates local stress fields that displace edge-dislocation cores.
Edge dislocations become more prevalent and less mobile in severely distorted BCC concentrated alloys than in conventional BCC alloys, where screw dislocations prevail.
Reduced dislocation mobility increases yield strength.
Reduced dislocation mobility alters plastic-deformation behavior.
A high-distortion alloy will have higher yield strength than a low-distortion BCC baseline.
A high-distortion alloy will exhibit a dislocation structure dominated by wavy edge dislocations relative to the baseline.
In situ neutron diffraction and resonant ultrasound methods can characterize elastic anisotropy in NbTaTiV.
In situ diffraction will reveal dislocation-density differences between the high- and low-distortion alloys.
The high-distortion alloy will have an elastic response distinct from that of the low-distortion baseline.
Single-phase BCC NbTaTiV remains phase-stable from room temperature to 900°C.
